A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe PVChat and include supplementary sections S1–S7. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the methods, equations, results, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original PVChat evaluations in Table 1, component ablations in Tables 2–4, supplementary token-count experiments, and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: v4 retains the original comparative evaluations, component ablations, supplementary token-count results, and qualitative single- and multi-character examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 and supplementary S4 retain the same augmentation pipeline, ReMoH routing, SPR/HAE losses, two-stage training, and multi-character masking.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same medical, TV-series, anime, and real-world scenarios, with existence, appearance, action, and location questions and the same single- and multi-character settings.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains InternVideo2 and VideoLLaMA2, while Table 2 retains the baseline and MoH comparisons. The newly cited depth-estimation work is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: The reference/query setup, eight-frame sampling, training budgets, baseline input procedures, and five evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.2 and supplementary S2/S4.

E4.justification: The ReMoH, loss, and data-component ablations in Tables 2–4, head-activation analysis in Figure 7, supplementary token sensitivity study, and qualitative case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and activation ratios without repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains PVChat accuracy 0.901 and BLEU 0.562, and supplementary Table 1 retains accuracy 0.922 for 16 tokens.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same mathematical development and Equations 1–11 for attention, routing, sparsity regularization, and the training objective. No formal assumptions or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same one-shot personalized video-understanding claim, proposed contributions, and claimed advantages over existing video models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning identity preservation, expert-head specialization, loss stabilization, and declining performance beyond 16 tokens are retained. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: v4 adds 'Code is at PVChat' with a GitHub repository hyperlink in the abstract; v2 lacks this code-access information. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and supplementary implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yan et al.'s Synthetic-to-real self-supervised robust depth estimation via learning with motion and structure priors as reference 56 in the introductory autonomous-driving passage. Existing references are retained with subsequent renumbering, and the research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short code-access sentence, and citation and version-header text is updated. The research narrative, section ordering, and supplementary organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence and reference cause limited text reflow, particularly in the abstract and bibliography. Figures and tables retain their content, design, and placement; supplementary pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository link provides a concrete implementation-access pointer absent from v2, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and all supplementary evidence remain unchanged, while the additional citation contributes little substantive benefit. The PDFs establish the access pointer, not the repository's completeness or usability.
